newsitem.title: UK: Major LME copper option trade a position switch.
newsitem.headline: Major LME copper option trade a position switch.

text.p: A significant turnover in London Metal Exchange (LME) copper traded options on Tuesday, when volume was over 203,000 lots, equivalent to some five million tonnes of metal, probably represents a position transfer or tax transaction, traders said.
There were some 77,000 calls and over 126,000 puts traded late on Tuesday. There has also been some further business today.
Traders said the operation could well be an inter-bank "give-up", where one bank transfers a range of positions on its book to another.

It could also be a end-year fiscal operation in Japan, possibly involving positions left over from Sumitomo's activities. Or, it may involve adjustments by another Asian operator believed to be active in options, they said.

LME officials were not available to comment on the trade on Wednesday. But in the past similar volumes have been reported when, for example, an option market-maker downgrades its activity to just customer business, and passes on its book to another market-maker.

Heavy call option volumes ranged from April 1997 monthly to the end of the year at strikes between $2,300 and $2,500 on the upside. Typical volumes were 4,000 lots at the $2,300 strike and in excess of 2,000 at $2,500.
In puts, the interest was at downside strikes between $2,000 and $2,200 - again stretching from April to December. Typical monthly volumes were 8,000 lots at $2,000 and 4,000 contracts at $2,200.
The LME April price is currently around $2,440 a tonne, with December near $2,200. So the calls involved are located in the money, while the puts are virtually all out-of-the-money,
Despite the size of the volumes passing through, traders do not expect the underlying market to be affected unduly, and there was little reaction on the LME on Wednesday.
"I don't think this is directional or influential. It is purely a switch," one said.
